title: Refund of a Twice-Paid TRICARE Prime First Installment - Calculation
content:
The duplicate refund on the first installment of a new fee-bearing **TRICARE Prime** enrollment returns the smaller of the latest payment posted against the first installment charge and its earlier payments together, less the refunds already issued against that latest payment, never more than the amount by which all of its payments exceed the installment's value less those refunds, that value being the whole annual fee of the enrollment's fee arrangement; the region keeps nothing of it on the account. The first installment charge is the installment charge whose coverage period begins on the enrollment's effective date. The duplicate refund is posted against the latest payment posted against the first installment charge and goes back through that payment's method. The annual fee of the enrollment's fee arrangement is the tier's annual individual fee for an individual arrangement and its annual family fee for a family arrangement.

1. **Excess** - all payments posted against the first installment charge, less the installment's value, never below zero, rounded to the cent.
2. **What comes off** - refunds already issued against the latest payment posted against the first installment charge come off both the payment the duplicate refund returns and its excess.
3. **Refund** - the payment it returns less what comes off it, never more than the excess less what comes off and less what the region keeps, never below zero, rounded to the cent.

A monthly figure of the annual fee is the annual fee divided by 12, and a quarterly figure the annual fee divided by 4, each rounded to the cent.

**Worked figure (hypothetical).** TRICARE Prime Retiree Group B, family arrangement (annual fee 969.36). Two payments of 969.36 stand against the charge beginning on the effective date, and nothing has been refunded: the excess is 969.36, the smaller of the latest payment and the earlier one is 969.36, and the refund is 969.36. Had 300.00 already been refunded against the latest payment, 300.00 would come off both the 969.36 returned and the 969.36 excess, and the refund would be 669.36.
